keys.rule: The version of the tool contract the tool is written for, "MAJOR.MINOR" — the SDK's MAJOR.MINOR. A Chest serves every version up to its own; an older Chest refuses the tool before reading anything else: "This tool needs a newer version of your Chest".

The tool's name and the label of its address: a lowercase letter, then up to 47 lowercase letters, digits or dashes; never login, node, documents, nor a name ending in -chest. Whoever installs the tool may give it another address.
Shown in lists: 1 to 48 printable characters.
Shown in the catalogue: 1 to 160 printable characters.
The tool's icon, a file of the chest/ directory: SVG or PNG, 64 KiB at most.
A picture of the tool for the catalogue, a file of the chest/ directory: PNG, JPEG or WebP, 512 KiB at most.
Optional long description: a local UTF-8 Markdown file, 32 KiB at most, never fetched from a URL. Render as text-based Markdown, never raw HTML; links only HTTP(S), no embedded remote media.
Ordered gallery: 1 to 6 distinct preview paths under chest/, each PNG, JPEG or WebP, 512 KiB at most. Without previews, the gallery uses preview if present; preview remains the list thumbnail.
The roles a member holds in the tool, the first the default: 1 to 16 distinct identifiers, each of the grammar of name. The tool is told each member's role; its own code decides what a role may do.
How declared roles are shown: an object giving roles of roles 1 to 40 printable characters each. Presentation only: never approved.
true for a part served to anyone on the Internet, on the tool's public host, outside /chest. Approved as a permission; closed at installation until whoever runs the tool opens it.

"tool": the public part sends its own Content-Security-Policy (a nonce per response, as Next.js needs), and the Chest adds beside it only its floor policy instead of its default one. Requires public; approved as a permission.

What the tool uses of its Chest, each at most once, each approved as a permission: database (its own PostgreSQL), sealed (values it seals, which only its members open through it; every version of the tool then waits for the owner or an admin), files (its private files), members (who has the tool), members.email (their addresses; with members), members.groups (every group of the Chest, and which of those members are in each; with members), notifications (badges and inbox items), ai (AI models through the Chest; with the key ai), folders (the folders of Files, the company's storage, that the owner or an admin gives the tool after it is installed; with the key folders), realtime (live updates to its members' open pages; its channels in the key realtime).

With the capability files: "maxObject", the largest object, a size such as "100 MiB" from 1 MiB to 512 MiB (32 MiB without it). No quota: the tool's files share the server's workload volume with every tool's, and a write is refused only when it is full (storage_full).

Required with the capability ai: "monthly", the whole euros a month the tool suggests, 1 to 1000 (5 without it; the owner's cap decides); "models", the aliases it calls among default, fast, smart, embedding, each once (default without it); "purpose", what it does with AI, 1 to 120 printable characters.

example.purpose: Summarises the tasks of a project

keys.rule: Required with the capability folders: "level", "view" (open and read the documents) or "edit" (also add and remove them), the most any folder given to the tool lets it do; "purpose", what it keeps there, 1 to 120 printable characters. Installing gives no folder: the owner or an admin gives each one from the tool's page. On a member's request (its Chest-Opener ticket) the tool reaches only what that member also sees.

With the capability realtime: the channels the members' pages join, and the tables whose writes become live events. "channels", 1 to 32 patterns, no channel name matched by two: "name", segments of ^[a-z0-9_-]{1,64}$ joined by colons, 128 characters at most, its last segment possibly {member} (the joining member's own id only), * (any segment) or {key} (a membership table decides); "join", absent for every member who has the tool, a list of the tool's roles, or {"table", "key", "member"} — a member joins {key} when a row of table has the key in column key and their id in column member (requires database; a row deleted removes them at once); "send" true lets those who join send ephemeral messages; "presence" true lets them appear in its presence. "feeds", up to 16: "table", whose inserts, updates and deletes become events <table>.insert, .update, .delete on "channel" — a declared channel, or prefix:{column} of a variable pattern, the column giving the last segment —, each carrying "columns" (1 to 32, the primary key first) of the row. Names of tables and columns are ^[a-z_][a-z0-9_]{0,62}$. Never approved: only the capability is.

The events the tool tells the other tools of the Chest, by type: two to four dotted words of lowercase letters, digits and dashes (64 characters at most; never member.*, access.* nor folders.*), each {"description", "data"} — what happened in a sentence of 1 to 80 printable characters, and every field its data carries with its kind: id, text, number, boolean, time, date, member, members, ? after the kind for an optional field (camelCase names; {} for none). Data with any other field is refused, 16 KiB at most. Each type approved as a permission, with the tools it reaches; a type's data only grows from one version to the next: a field is never removed, retyped nor made optional — a new shape is a new type.

The events posted to POST /chest-events: "member.*", the members' lifecycle (requires the capability members), and event types, from whichever other tool emits them — never the tool's own events. Each approved as a permission, with the tools it comes from.

What Perseus may read and do in the tool, 1 to 16, by name: one to three words of lowercase letters and digits joined by dashes (48 characters at most), each {"description", "input", "changes"} — what it does in a sentence a member reads in Perseus's proposal, 1 to 80 printable characters; every field of its input with its kind: id, text, number, boolean, time, date, member, members, document, amount, ? after the kind for an optional field (camelCase names, up to 16; {} for none), a document being a link to a document of Files the member may read, which the tool opens once, an amount {"value": "240.00", "currency": "GBP"} (ISO 4217); "changes", false for an action that only reads, which Perseus calls by itself, true for one Perseus only proposes and the member's Confirm calls. The Chest posts {"input": {…}} (64 KiB at most) to POST /chest-actions/<name>, signed (Chest-Action) and in the member's name (Chest-Member), with an input of exactly that shape, and waits 10 seconds for {"said", "data"}: the sentence Perseus shows, and what a read returns (64 KiB at most). Each action approved as a permission.

add-paper.description: Add a paper to a section of the company

keys.rule: With the capability folders: the sections of the tool that take papers, 1 to 16, by key (the grammar of an action's name), each {"name", "folder"} — how it is shown (1 to 40 printable characters) and the folder of Files given to the tool that keeps its papers (1 to 80) — and an optional "action", a declared action that changes and takes a required document, which the mail room calls once it filed a paper there, in the reviewer's name: its document field the paper, a text field named section the section's key, and each other field named as a value read (due, date, issuer, reference) of its kind. The mail room offers them beside the folders of Files, to whoever can edit that folder with the tool. Never approved: the tool only reaches the folders it is given.

Work the tool does by itself at set times, 1 to 8: each {"name", "cron"} — a name of its own (^[a-z][a-z0-9-]{0,31}$) and a five-field cron line (minute hour day month weekday: numbers, *, ranges, lists and steps, one space apart, Sunday 0 or 7, no names nor macros) read on the wall clock of the Chest's time zone, its runs 15 minutes apart at least. Each run is posted, signed, to POST /chest-schedules, the tool woken if it sleeps, and answered within 5 minutes. Each schedule approved as a permission; running by itself is what is approved.

The hosts the server reaches on the Internet, 1 to 32, none covered by another: a host name, *.domain for every name under it, or * alone for any host. Each approved as a permission. Without it, the tool reaches nothing.

The names of the variables the tool expects, 1 to 32 distinct: never PORT, HOME, PATH, HTTP_PROXY, HTTPS_PROXY, ALL_PROXY, NO_PROXY, nor a name starting with CHEST_, NODE_, NPM_. Whoever runs the tool sets their values in the Chest, never in the code.
How the Chest builds and starts the tool: fixed commands run as argument vectors, never through a shell.
"node": the Chest's pinned Node image.
"npm ci": exactly what package-lock.json says, which is required at the root.
The build, "npm run <script>"; none without it.
"npm start" or "npm run <script>".
The port the server listens on, 1024 to 65535; the Chest sets PORT to it.
The path prefixes of built files, served as they are on both hosts: up to 4, each "/…/" (/_next/static/ without it); never /chest/, /_chest/, /chest-events/, /chest-schedules/ or /chest-actions/.

refused: node_modules, anywhere: the Chest installs the dependencies from package-lock.json
a symbolic or hard link, a device, a socket or a pipe
.git, and a Dockerfile, Containerfile, .dockerignore or .containerignore directory at the root
extended attributes, and a path that leaves the tree

migrations.rule: Played in the order of their names, each once, as one simple query in a transaction of its own, as the tool's database role: the owner of its database, not a superuser. Only with the capability database. UTF-8 SQL text without NUL; a migration played is never changed: a change is a new one. Expand, then contract: the version in service runs on the new schema while the next one starts, and after a rollback without its data, so a migration only adds; what a version stops reading is dropped, renamed or retyped by the release after it, in a migration marked with the line "-- chest: contract" (chest check warns about any other).

policies.public: default-src 'self'; script-src 'self'; style-src 'self'; img-src 'self' data: blob:; font-src 'self'; connect-src 'self'; object-src 'none'; base-uri 'self'; form-action 'self'; frame-ancestors 'none'
